progression.note: Hit the top of the rep range for all sets, two sessions in a row, before adding load or reps. If you miss the bottom of the range, repeat the same weight next time.

deload.note: Every 4th week: cut sets to ~60%, load to ~90%, and cardio minutes to ~70% of normal. Keep the same exercises and rep ranges; this is a recovery week, not a day off.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.gym: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell vertically at chest height; squat between a squat rack or in open floor space.
exercises.home: Same movement with a dumbbell or kettlebell held at the chest; a loaded backpack works if you have no weights.
exercises.cue: Elbows inside knees at the bottom, chest tall, drive through the whole foot.
exercises.startHint: Pick a weight you could squat for about 12 reps with 2-3 reps left in reserve.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.gym: Flat bench, one dumbbell in each hand, press from chest to lockout.
exercises.home: Press dumbbells lying on a sturdy bench, bench press pad, or on the floor (reduced range of motion).
exercises.cue: Shoulder blades pulled back and down, control the lowering phase.
exercises.startHint: Pick dumbbells you could press for about 12 reps with 2-3 left in reserve.

exercises.name: Row (Seated Cable / DB Row)
exercises.gym: Seated cable row machine, chest up, pull handle to the lower ribs.
exercises.home: Single-arm dumbbell row braced on a bench or chair, or a resistance band anchored to a door.
exercises.cue: Lead with the elbow, squeeze the shoulder blade, avoid shrugging.
exercises.startHint: Pick a load or band tension you could row for about 12 reps with 2-3 left in reserve.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift (DB) / Hip Hinge
exercises.gym: Dumbbells in front of thighs, hinge at the hips keeping a flat back, lower to mid-shin.
exercises.home: Same with dumbbells or a kettlebell, or a bodyweight hip hinge if no load is available.
exercises.cue: Push hips back first, soft knees, feel the hamstrings stretch, not the lower back.
exercises.startHint: Pick a load you could hinge for about 12 reps with 2-3 left in reserve, lighter than your squat.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown / Assisted Pull-Up
exercises.gym: Cable lat pulldown machine, pull the bar to the upper chest.
exercises.home: Band-assisted pull-up on a bar (loop a band over the bar and under a knee/foot), or banded pulldown from a high anchor.
exercises.cue: Pull elbows down and back, chest up, avoid swinging.
exercises.startHint: Pick a machine weight or band thickness that lets you complete about 10-12 reps with 2-3 left in reserve.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.gym: Forearm plank on a mat, body in one straight line.
exercises.home: Same on any floor; elevate hands on a couch edge if the floor is too hard on elbows.
exercises.cue: Squeeze glutes, pull ribs down, don't let hips sag or pike.
exercises.startHint: Start with a hold you can keep with perfect form, stopping a few seconds before you'd break form.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.gym: On your back on a mat, opposite arm/leg lower and extend while keeping the low back flat.
exercises.home: Same on any floor or carpeted surface.
exercises.cue: Press low back into the floor the whole set, move slowly.
exercises.startHint: Start with a rep count per side you can do with a flat low back throughout, 2-3 reps short of failure.

exercises.name: Barbell Back Squat
exercises.gym: Squat rack, bar on upper traps, squat to at least thigh-parallel.
exercises.home: Substitute heavy goblet squat or double kettlebell front squat — no safe home barbell squat alternative.
exercises.cue: Brace the core, knees track over toes, drive up through mid-foot.
exercises.startHint: Start with an empty bar or light plates until form is solid, then add small jumps.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.gym: Flat bench in a rack with safety pins or a spotter, bar to mid-chest.
exercises.home: Substitute heavy dumbbell bench press — avoid an unracked home barbell bench without a spotter.
exercises.cue: Shoulder blades set, slight arch, bar path straight down to the chest.
exercises.startHint: Start light enough to control the bar for all reps with a spotter or safety pins set.

exercises.name: Barbell Deadlift
exercises.gym: Bar on the floor, hinge down, flat back, pull bar close to the shins.
exercises.home: Substitute heavy double-kettlebell or dumbbell deadlift.
exercises.cue: Take the slack out of the bar first, push the floor away, lock out hips and knees together.
exercises.startHint: Start light, well under your squat weight, and focus on a flat back before adding load.

exercises.name: Barbell Overhead Press
exercises.gym: Bar from the rack or floor, press straight overhead, lock out above the ears.
exercises.home: Substitute standing dumbbell shoulder press.
exercises.cue: Brace the core, squeeze glutes, don't lean back excessively.
exercises.startHint: Start light — this lift is usually your weakest main lift; pick a load for about 8 clean reps.

exercises.name: Barbell Row
exercises.gym: Hinge over the bar, pull to the lower ribs, control the descent.
exercises.home: Substitute heavy double-dumbbell row or a band row with a strong anchor.
exercises.cue: Flat back the whole set, pull with the elbows not the hands.
exercises.startHint: Pick a load you can pull for about 8-10 reps while keeping the back flat.

exercises.name: Pull-Up
exercises.gym: Dead hang on a pull-up bar, pull chin over the bar, full extension at the bottom.
exercises.home: Same on a doorway or outdoor pull-up bar; use a resistance band for assistance if needed.
exercises.cue: Pull elbows down toward the hips, avoid kipping.
exercises.startHint: If you can't do a full rep yet, use enough band assistance to get 5-8 clean reps and remove assistance over time.

exercises.name: Hanging Knee Raise
exercises.gym: Hang from a pull-up bar, raise knees toward the chest without swinging.
exercises.home: Same on an outdoor bar; substitute lying leg raises on the floor if no bar is available.
exercises.cue: Curl the pelvis under at the top, lower under control.
exercises.startHint: Start with a rep count you can do without swinging, 2-3 reps short of failure.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Swing
exercises.gym: Hip-hinge swing of a kettlebell between the legs to chest/shoulder height.
exercises.home: Same with a kettlebell or a heavy dumbbell held with both hands.
exercises.cue: Power comes from the hip snap, not the arms or low back.
exercises.startHint: Pick a kettlebell light enough that your hinge technique stays clean for the full set.

exercises.name: Farmer's Carry
exercises.gym: Carry a heavy kettlebell or dumbbell in each hand, walk a set distance or time.
exercises.home: Same with dumbbells, kettlebells, or heavy loaded bags; use a hallway, yard, or outdoor path.
exercises.cue: Stand tall, shoulders back, don't let the loads pull you to one side.
exercises.startHint: Pick a load you can carry with perfect posture for the full time, stopping before your grip or form fails.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.gym: Adjustable bench set to a slight incline, press dumbbells from chest to lockout.
exercises.home: Prop one end of a sturdy bench/cushion stack, or do floor press if no incline is available.
exercises.cue: Keep wrists stacked over elbows, control the eccentric.
exercises.startHint: Pick dumbbells slightly lighter than your flat bench press for about 10-12 reps.

exercises.name: Walking Lunge
exercises.gym: Step forward into a lunge, alternate legs walking down the gym floor; hold dumbbells for extra load if needed.
exercises.home: Same across a yard, hallway, or outdoor space; hold water bottles or a backpack for load.
exercises.cue: Front knee tracks over the foot, torso stays tall, push through the front heel to stand.
exercises.startHint: Start with a rep count per leg you can do with good knee control, 2-3 reps short of failure.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.gym: Standard push-up on the gym floor; elevate hands on a bench if needed to regress.
exercises.home: Same on any floor; elevate hands on a couch, step, or wall to regress as needed.
exercises.cue: Straight line from shoulders to ankles, elbows at about 45 degrees.
exercises.startHint: Use an incline (hands on a bench/couch) if needed to get 8-12 clean reps, then progress to the floor.

exercises.name: Mountain Climbers
exercises.gym: From a high plank, drive knees alternately toward the chest at pace.
exercises.home: Same on any floor space.
exercises.cue: Keep hips low and level, hands stay planted under shoulders.
exercises.startHint: Start with a duration at a pace you can sustain with good plank position throughout.

exercises.name: Burpee
exercises.gym: Squat, hands down, jump feet back to plank, optional push-up, jump feet in, jump up.
exercises.home: Same anywhere with floor space; drop the push-up or the jump to regress.
exercises.cue: Move with control on the way down, land softly on the jump.
exercises.startHint: Start with a rep count at a pace you can hold with good form for every rep.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.gym: Forearm side plank on a mat, hips lifted and stacked.
exercises.home: Same on any floor.
exercises.cue: Stack shoulder over elbow, push hips up and forward, don't let them sag.
exercises.startHint: Start with a hold per side you can keep with hips fully lifted, stopping a few seconds before form breaks.

exercises.name: Step-Up
exercises.gym: Step onto a flat bench or box, drive through the lead leg to stand tall, step down with control.
exercises.home: Use a sturdy outdoor step, porch stair, or low wall.
exercises.cue: Drive through the heel of the stepping leg, avoid pushing off the trailing foot.
exercises.startHint: Start with a step height and rep count per leg you can do with full control, 2-3 reps short of failure.

sessions.title: Full Body A
sessions.notes: Foundation full-body day: squat and push emphasis. Rest 60-90s between sets, focus on learning the movement before adding load.

sessions.title: Full Body B
sessions.notes: Foundation full-body day: hinge and pull emphasis, plus core.

sessions.title: Full Body C
sessions.notes: Foundation full-body day: squat, pull and hinge together, lighter press load.

sessions.title: Walk-Run Intervals
sessions.notes: Easy aerobic base-building session. Stay conversational on the walk portions.

cardio.instructions: 5 min warm-up walk, then alternate 2 min easy jog / 2 min walk for the remainder, finish with a 3 min cool-down walk.

sessions.title: Barbell A
sessions.notes: Introduces the barbell squat and bench as the two main lifts; keep technique priority over load.

sessions.title: Barbell B
sessions.notes: Deadlift and overhead press day; deadlift technique comes before load.

sessions.title: Barbell C
sessions.notes: Squat and bench again with a higher rep range, plus a short KB/bodyweight finisher.

sessions.title: Zone 2 Run
sessions.notes: Steady aerobic run or brisk walk-run. You should be able to hold a conversation.

cardio.instructions: Continuous easy-pace run or fast walk, nasal breathing if possible, no sprinting.

sessions.title: Sprint Intervals
sessions.notes: Higher-intensity conditioning; outdoor space or a track works well.

cardio.instructions: 5 min warm-up jog, then 6 rounds of 30s hard effort / 90s easy walk recovery, 5 min cool-down walk.

sessions.title: Build B
sessions.notes: Deadlift/press/pull-up day; pull-ups replace lat pulldown as strength allows.

sessions.title: Build C
sessions.notes: Accessory-focused day adding lunges and incline press for balance and extra volume.

sessions.title: Long Zone 2 Run
sessions.notes: Longer aerobic base run; pace stays easy throughout, this is about duration not speed.

cardio.instructions: Continuous easy-pace run or fast walk for the full duration, conversational effort.

sessions.title: Sprint Intervals (Build)
sessions.notes: Extended version of the earlier sprint session.

cardio.instructions: 5 min warm-up jog, then 8 rounds of 30s hard effort / 90s easy walk recovery, 5 min cool-down walk.

sessions.title: Full-Body Conditioning Circuit
sessions.notes: As many rounds as possible of the listed moves, keeping form solid throughout; rest as needed.

sessions.title: Long Ruck
sessions.notes: Outdoor loaded carry walk; use a backpack with weight plates, books, or bottles.

cardio.instructions: Walk outdoors for the full duration carrying 8-10kg in a backpack, upright posture, steady pace.

phases.title: Foundation
phases.focus: Learn the core movement patterns (squat, press, pull, hinge, core) with light to moderate load, and build a basic aerobic habit.

phases.title: Barbell Initiation
phases.focus: Introduce the barbell squat, bench, deadlift, overhead press and row; add a dedicated aerobic run and a higher-intensity interval session.

phases.title: Build
phases.focus: Increase strength volume, add a dedicated conditioning circuit and a longer aerobic run, and introduce rucking for loaded-carry endurance.

ladder.title: Cold Shower Finish - 30s
ladder.detail: End your normal shower with 30 seconds of cold water. Breathe slowly and steadily; step out immediately if you feel faint or your skin goes numb/painful rather than just cold.

ladder.title: Cold Shower Finish - 60s
ladder.detail: End your normal shower with 60 seconds of cold water, same breathing focus as before. Stop early if you feel dizzy, chest tightness, or numbness beyond cold.

ladder.title: Cold Shower Finish - 90s
ladder.detail: End your shower with 90 seconds of cold water. Keep breaths slow and even; exit if you feel faint, can't catch your breath, or skin loses sensation.

ladder.title: Cold Shower Finish - 2 min
ladder.detail: End your shower with 2 minutes of cold water. Stop immediately if dizzy, short of breath, or in pain beyond normal cold discomfort.

ladder.title: Cold Shower Finish - 3 min
ladder.detail: End your shower with 3 minutes of cold water, the top of this track. Never attempt this alone if you have a heart condition; exit at the first sign of dizziness or numbness.

ladder.title: Phone-Free First Hour
ladder.detail: Leave your phone in another room for the first hour after waking. Use the time for movement, sunlight, or a quiet routine instead.

ladder.title: 14-Hour Fasting Window
ladder.detail: Keep all food within a 10-hour daily window (e.g. 9am-7pm), 14 hours fasted. Drink water freely; stop and eat if you feel dizzy, shaky, or unwell, and skip this on your hardest training days if it hurts your performance.

ladder.title: 16-Hour Fasting Window
ladder.detail: Keep all food within an 8-hour daily window, 16 hours fasted. Water and black coffee/tea are fine; stop eating window rules if dizzy or unwell, and avoid this on heavy barbell training days if energy suffers.

ladder.title: 18-Hour Fasting Window
ladder.detail: Keep all food within a 6-hour daily window, 18 hours fasted. Stay well hydrated with water/electrolytes; stop if dizzy, lightheaded, or unwell, and skip entirely on your heaviest lifting or longest run days.

ladder.title: No Added-Sugar Day
ladder.detail: Go a full day with no added sugar: no sweets, sugary drinks, or desserts. Whole fruit is fine.

ladder.title: Early Wake - 06:30
ladder.detail: Be out of bed by 06:30. Set a fixed bedtime the night before so you get at least 7 hours of sleep; don't chase this goal by cutting sleep short.

ladder.title: Early Wake - 06:00
ladder.detail: Be out of bed by 06:00, with a fixed bedtime the night before protecting at least 7 hours of sleep.

ladder.title: 10 Minutes Morning Sunlight
ladder.detail: Get outside within an hour of waking for at least 10 minutes of natural daylight, no sunglasses. Cloudy days still count.

ladder.title: Cold Shower + Calm Breathing
ladder.detail: During a cold shower finish, add slow 4-second-in/6-second-out breathing the whole time instead of gasping. Exit immediately if you feel dizzy or your breathing can't settle.

ladder.title: Ruck - 30 min / 5kg
ladder.detail: Walk outdoors for 30 minutes carrying 5kg in a backpack, upright posture. Stop if you feel sharp joint pain.

ladder.title: Ruck - 45 min / 8kg
ladder.detail: Walk outdoors for 45 minutes carrying 8kg in a backpack, steady pace, good posture. Stop if you feel sharp joint pain.

ladder.title: Ruck - 60 min / 10kg
ladder.detail: Walk outdoors for 60 minutes carrying 10kg in a backpack, steady pace, good posture throughout. Stop if you feel sharp joint pain.

ladder.title: One Hour of Silence
ladder.detail: Spend one hour with no music, podcasts, TV, or notifications — just you and the task at hand or a quiet walk.

ladder.title: 24-Hour Digital Sabbath
ladder.detail: Go 24 hours with no social media, streaming, or non-essential phone use. Tell people in advance so urgent contact can still reach you by call if truly needed.

ladder.title: Nightly Gratitude Journal
ladder.detail: Before bed, write down three specific things that went well that day. Two or three sentences is enough.
